requirements.original: Values or templates may be assigned to variables or template variables (see clause 11).
requirements.canonical: A value MAY be assigned to a variable and a template MAY be assigned to a template variable.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear pairing of 'values or templates' with 'variables or template variables'; chosen the respective pairing (templates only to template variables, consistent with restriction b), values also to template variables per clause 11.
readings: A value MAY be assigned to a variable and a template MAY be assigned to a template variable.
A value or a template MAY be assigned to either a variable or a template variable.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Values or templates may be assigned to variables or template variables (see clause 11).

requirements.original: This is indicated by the symbol ":=". Values or templates may be assigned to variables or template variables (see clause 11).
requirements.canonical: An assignment IS denoted by the symbol `:=`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- This is indicated by the symbol ":=". Values or templates may be assigned to variables or template variables (see clause 11).

requirements.original: ValueRef ":=" ( Expression | TemplateBody )
requirements.canonical: An assignment has the syntax ValueRef `:=` followed by either an Expression or a TemplateBody.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- ValueRef ":=" ( Expression | TemplateBody )

requirements.original: During execution of an assignment, the right-hand side of the assignment shall evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: During execution of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- During execution of an assignment, the right-hand side of the assignment shall evaluate to a value or template that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: The effect of an assignment is to bind the variable to the value of the expression or to a template.
requirements.canonical: The effect of an assignment IS to bind the variable on the left hand side to the value of the expression or to a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- The effect of an assignment is to bind the variable to the value of the expression or to a template.

requirements.original: Assignments use the rules of passing by value.
requirements.canonical: An assignment uses the rules of passing by value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Assignments use the rules of passing by value.

requirements.original: If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.
requirements.canonical: If the assigned variable is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference IS copied by the assignment and the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) IS NOT copied.
requirements.condition: the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.

requirements.original: In all other cases, the content being assigned shall be a copy of the evaluated right-hand side. If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.
requirements.canonical: If the assigned variable is not of an object reference type, the content being assigned SHALL be a copy of the evaluated right hand side.
requirements.condition: the variable is not of a type whose values are object references
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- In all other cases, the content being assigned shall be a copy of the evaluated right-hand side. If the variable being assigned is of a type whose values are object references, only the reference is copied, but the referenced object (e.g. component, timer or port) is not.

requirements.original: Assignments are processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.
requirements.canonical: An assignment IS processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Assignments are processed from left to right, i.e. expressions in the left hand side are evaluated before those in the right hand side.

requirements.original: The evaluations obey the operator precedence defined in table 6.
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of an assignment SHALL obey the operator precedence defined in table 6.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- The evaluations obey the operator precedence defined in table 6.

requirements.original: Unless the assignment is to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter, the right hand side is evaluated completely before the resulting value or template is bound to the evaluated left-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: Unless the assignment is to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter, the right hand side IS evaluated completely before the resulting value or template is bound to the evaluated left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.condition: the assignment is not to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Unless the assignment is to a lazy or fuzzy variable or parameter, the right hand side is evaluated completely before the resulting value or template is bound to the evaluated left-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: Whenever assignments are used within the right hand side of an assignment (due to assignment notation), these rules apply recursively.
requirements.canonical: When assignments are used within the right hand side of an assignment (due to assignment notation), the assignment evaluation rules apply recursively.
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used within the right hand side
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Whenever assignments are used within the right hand side of an assignment (due to assignment notation), these rules apply recursively.

requirements.original: A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.
requirements.canonical: A structured value on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL be assigned completely to the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.

requirements.original: A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.
requirements.canonical: If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, the fields uninitialized at the right hand side SHALL also become uninitialized at the left hand side.
requirements.condition: a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- A structured value on the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned completely to the variable on the left-hand side of the assignment, If a partially initialized value is assigned to a completely initialized variable, fields uninitialized at the right-hand side of the assignment shall also become uninitialized at the left-hand side.

requirements.original: When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.
requirements.canonical: When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable SHALL be evaluated as much as necessary before the assignment, i.e. an ancestor of that element or field initialized with a function call SHALL be evaluated.
requirements.condition: a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.

requirements.original: Thus, if the variable is fully assigned, it does not need to be evaluated before assignment. When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy variable is fully assigned, the variable NEED NOT be evaluated before the assignment.
requirements.condition: the lazy or fuzzy variable is fully assigned
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Thus, if the variable is fully assigned, it does not need to be evaluated before assignment. When a direct or indirect element or field of a lazy or fuzzy variable is assigned, the variable is also evaluated as much as necessary before assignment, i.e. if an ancestor of that element or field is initialized with a function call, it shall be evaluated.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Table 17: Overview of TTCN-3 basic program statements: Leaving a loop, alt, altstep or interleave; Col2: break

requirements.canonical: The logging statement IS denoted by the keyword `log`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Table 17: Overview of TTCN-3 basic program statements: Logging; Col2: log

requirements.original: NOTE: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor which was formerly assigned a function call, this function call will be evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.
requirements.canonical: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor formerly assigned a function call, the function call IS evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.
requirements.condition: a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable with an ancestor formerly assigned a function call is assigned
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- NOTE: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor which was formerly assigned a function call, this function call will be evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.

requirements.original: Thus, the other sub-fields and sub-elements of that ancestor, apart from the field or element being assigned become non-fuzzy. NOTE: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor which was formerly assigned a function call, this function call will be evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.
requirements.canonical: After such an assignment, the other sub-fields and sub-elements of that ancestor, apart from the field or element being assigned, become non-fuzzy.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- Thus, the other sub-fields and sub-elements of that ancestor, apart from the field or element being assigned become non-fuzzy. NOTE: If a sub-field or sub-element of a fuzzy variable is assigned that has an ancestor which was formerly assigned a function call, this function call will be evaluated once before the assignment and replaced by its result inside the variable.

requirements.original: a) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to a value, template, port or timer which is type compatible with the variable at the left-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of an assignment SHALL evaluate to a value, template, port or timer which is type compatible with the variable at the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- a) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to a value, template, port or timer which is type compatible with the variable at the left-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: b) When the right-hand side of the assignment evaluates to a template (global or local template, in-line template, template variable or a matching mechanism), the variable at the left hand side shall be a template variable.
requirements.canonical: When the right hand side of an assignment evaluates to a template (global or local template, in-line template, template variable or matching mechanism), the left hand side of the assignment SHALL be a template variable.
requirements.condition: the right hand side evaluates to a template
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- b) When the right-hand side of the assignment evaluates to a template (global or local template, in-line template, template variable or a matching mechanism), the variable at the left hand side shall be a template variable.

requirements.original: c) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of an assignment SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- c) The right-hand side of an assignment shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: d) If the left-hand side of the assignment is a reference to a non-optional value object (i.e. a value definition, a mandatory field, a record/set of/array element, a union alternative, a value parameter), the right-hand side shall not be a reference to an omitted field or the omit symbol.
requirements.canonical: If the left hand side of an assignment is a reference to a non-optional value object (a value definition, a mandatory field, a record/set of/array element, a union alternative or a value parameter), the right hand side SHALL NOT be a reference to an omitted field or the `omit` symbol.
requirements.condition: the left hand side is a reference to a non-optional value object
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- d) If the left-hand side of the assignment is a reference to a non-optional value object (i.e. a value definition, a mandatory field, a record/set of/array element, a union alternative, a value parameter), the right-hand side shall not be a reference to an omitted field or the omit symbol.

requirements.original: e) Using a reference to an omitted field in the right-hand side of the assignment has the same effect as using the omit keyword.
requirements.canonical: Using a reference to an omitted field in the right hand side of an assignment has the same effect as using the `omit` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.1 -- e) Using a reference to an omitted field in the right-hand side of the assignment has the same effect as using the omit keyword.

requirements.original: In addition to the basic assignments it is possible to use shorthand assignments for integer variables that shall be incremented by 1 or decremented by 1.
requirements.canonical: A shorthand assignment MAY be used for an integer variable that is incremented by 1 or decremented by 1.

examples.text: var integer v_j; for (v_j:=1; v_j<=10; v_j++) { … }; // increments v_j after each iteration v_j--; // decrements the variable v_j

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.2 -- In addition to the basic assignments it is possible to use shorthand assignments for integer variables that shall be incremented by 1 or decremented by 1.

requirements.original: The statement "v_integer++" is a shorthand form of "v_integer ;= v_integer + 1" and the statement "v_integer--" is a shorthand form of "v_integer := v_integer – 1".
requirements.canonical: The statement `v_integer++` IS a shorthand form of `v_integer := v_integer + 1`.

ambiguity.issue: Typo in the source: ';=' is written instead of the assignment symbol ':='.

examples.text: var integer v_j; for (v_j:=1; v_j<=10; v_j++) { … }; // increments v_j after each iteration v_j--; // decrements the variable v_j

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.2 -- The statement "v_integer++" is a shorthand form of "v_integer ;= v_integer + 1" and the statement "v_integer--" is a shorthand form of "v_integer := v_integer – 1".

requirements.original: The statement "v_integer++" is a shorthand form of "v_integer ;= v_integer + 1" and the statement "v_integer--" is a shorthand form of "v_integer := v_integer – 1".
requirements.canonical: The statement `v_integer--` IS a shorthand form of `v_integer := v_integer - 1`.

examples.text: var integer v_j; for (v_j:=1; v_j<=10; v_j++) { … }; // increments v_j after each iteration v_j--; // decrements the variable v_j

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.1.2 -- The statement "v_integer++" is a shorthand form of "v_integer ;= v_integer + 1" and the statement "v_integer--" is a shorthand form of "v_integer := v_integer – 1".

requirements.original: if "(" [ ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" ] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock { else if "(" [ ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" ] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock } [ else StatementBlock]
requirements.canonical: The if-else statement has the syntax `if (` [ (VarInstance | Assignment) `;` ] BooleanExpression `)` StatementBlock, followed by zero or more `else if (` [ (VarInstance | Assignment) `;` ] BooleanExpression `)` StatementBlock, optionally followed by `else` StatementBlock.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- if "(" [ ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" ] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock { else if "(" [ ( VarInstance | Assignment ) ";" ] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock } [ else StatementBlock]

requirements.original: NOTE 1: `else if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] is a shorthand notation for_ `else "{" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] "}"._
requirements.canonical: The notation `else if (BooleanExpression) StatementBlock [else StatementBlock]` IS a shorthand notation for `else { if (BooleanExpression) StatementBlock [else StatementBlock] }`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- NOTE 1: `else if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] is a shorthand notation for_ `else "{" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else` _StatementBlock] "}"._

requirements.original: NOTE 2: if "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [else _StatementBlock] is a shorthand_ notation for **"{" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else** _StatementBlock] "}"._
requirements.canonical: The notation `if ((VarInstance | Assignment); BooleanExpression) StatementBlock [else StatementBlock]` IS a shorthand notation for `{ (VarInstance | Assignment); if (BooleanExpression) StatementBlock [else StatementBlock] }`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- NOTE 2: if "(" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [else _StatementBlock] is a shorthand_ notation for **"{" (VarInstance | Assignment) ";" if "(" BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock [ else** _StatementBlock] "}"._

requirements.original: The branching of the control flow is decided upon the value of the Boolean expressions - the condition.
requirements.canonical: The branching of the control flow of an if-else statement IS decided upon the value of the boolean expressions (the conditions).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- The branching of the control flow is decided upon the value of the Boolean expressions - the condition.

requirements.original: A statement block - and only one - will be executed, if its condition evaluates to true.
requirements.canonical: Exactly one statement block of an if-else statement IS executed, namely the first one (in textual order) whose condition evaluates to true.

ambiguity.issue: The text does not state which block is executed when several conditions evaluate to true, nor that conditions are evaluated in order; chosen the conventional reading (first true condition in textual order), which follows from the shorthand in NOTE 1.
readings: Exactly one statement block IS executed, namely the first one in textual order whose condition evaluates to true.
At most one statement block IS executed, which is one whose condition evaluates to true (selection unspecified).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- A statement block - and only one - will be executed, if its condition evaluates to true.

requirements.original: The optional else specifies a statement block that will be executed if all the "if" and "else if" conditions before are false.
requirements.canonical: The statement block of the optional `else` branch IS executed if all preceding `if` and `else if` conditions are false.
requirements.condition: all preceding if and else if conditions are false
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- The optional else specifies a statement block that will be executed if all the "if" and "else if" conditions before are false.

requirements.original: Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.canonical: A boolean expression of an if-else statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.original: Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.canonical: An init statement of an if-else statement IS executed before the boolean expression it precedes is evaluated.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- Boolean expressions may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the if-statement, including its else branch.
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within an init statement SHALL be limited to the if-else statement, including its else branches.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.2 -- The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the if-statement, including its else branch.
